The '''Farstrider Lodge''' (or '''Farstrider's Lodge''') is a hunters' lodge located in southeastern [[Loch Modan]] and formerly the starting area for [[High elf (playable)|high elves]] until [[patch 1.17.1]], after which it was replaced with the [[Thalassian Highlands]]. It houses several merchants and quest givers, as well as a hunter trainer and a pet trainer.

The Farstrider Lodge was host to a caravan of high elven refugees travelling to Stormwind that have been waylaid by an attack by the dark iron dwarves of Shadowforge.

==Patch changes==
* [[File:Expansion_logo_mysteriesofazeroth.png|40px]] '''[[Patch 1.17.1]] (2023-12-20):''' No longer the high elf starting area.
* [[File:Expansion_logo_mysteriesofazeroth.png|40px]] '''[[Patch 1.17.0]] (2023-10-03):''' The Farstrider Lodge is getting a new look! More accurate to its High Elven legacy. The gilded exterior blending with the natural wilds showcases both the ancestral ties to the Kaldorei, as well as the pride and progress of their civilization before the coming of the Scourge.

Lady '''Farenia Roseheart''' is a current member of the [[Regency Council]] of [[Alah'Thalas]]. The youngest member of the Council, she is a staunch supporter of [[Vereesa Windrunner]], being the only member of the Council to vote in her favor when Lord [[Astalor Sunsworn]] made a motion to be named Lord-Regent of Quel'Thalas following the retaking of [[Shalandis Isle]].<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u90BCZfygz0 A GOOD DAY — Everlook Broadcasting Co. Radio Play Series]</ref>

==Quotes==
;Gossip
Loathe though I am to do this to her, it seems that despite her best efforts Vereesa has not been able to handle her responsibilities on her own. For the good of our people we must look to someone else for leadership.

Sadly, some here cling to the past, hindering our progress. Perhaps the responsibility of the crown is too much for one head in these circumstances, yet reluctance is ever the companion of fear of change.

We must put our people first and cast aside antiquated loyalties to usher in a new, better era.

{{Npcbox | name = Father Lycan | image = Father Lycan.png | title = Herald of Vorgendor | level = ?? | type = Boss | faction = Boss | aggro = {{Aggro|-1|-1}} | race = Worgen | creature = Humanoid | gender = Male | location = [[Circle of Power]], [[Hyjal]] | status = Killable }} '''Father Lycan''' is a [[worgen]] pricolich and bloodmage who ventured to the world of Azeroth from the worgen homeworld of [[Vorgendor]]. After crawling over the [[Greymane Wall]] into [[Gilneas]] from the [[Silverpine Forest]], he introduced [[Celia Harlow|Celia]] and [[Mortimer Harlow]] to the blood magics that they used to corrupt the nobility and leadership of the human nation.[[Celia's Journal]] As part of a bid to purify the [[Scythe of Elune]], [[Arch Druid Dreamwind]] directs adventurers to kill the pricoliches on Azeroth so that their influence in the world wanes. In the [[Circle of Power]] of [[Mount Hyjal]], the Arch Druid directs adventurers to summon Father Lycan by speaking his name with an arcane orb infused with the essence of primal magic in order to ensnare him and strip away his dark powers, rendering him vulnerable. ==Abilities== * '''Flame of Vorgendor''' — Calls down a pillar of fire, burning all enemies within the area for 3600 Fire damage and an additional 18000 Fire damage over 15 seconds. * '''Doombolt''' — Sends a shadowy bolt at the enemy, causing 25000 Shadow damage. * '''Herald's Transmutation''' — Transforms an enemy into a Shadowfang Glutton, enslaving it to the caster's will for 15 seconds. ==Quotes== ;Aggro :'''Father Lycan yells:''' You have dared to summon me? I shall bring doom to this world, for I am herald of Vorgendor! ;Herald's Transmutation :'''Father Lycan yells:''' Bask in my power! ;50% :'''Father Lycan yells:''' I shall bring forth a new reality... ;Kill :'''Father Lycan yells:''' Behold, the doom of Vorgendor! ;Death :'''Father Lycan yells:''' The power of Vorgendor, I can feel it fading... ==Objective of== * {{questlong|Neutral|60R|Pricolich Lycan}} ==Patch changes== * {{Patch|1.17.2|note=Added.}} ==References== {{reflist}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Lycan}} [[Category:Worgen characters]] [[Category:Hyjal mobs]] [[Category:World bosses]]

The '''Farstriders''', also known as the '''Elven Ranger Corps''', are a high elven organization that encompasses the elven rangers of [[Quel'Thalas (kingdom)|Quel'Thalas]], masters of marksmanship and scouting. It was charged with the defense of Quel'Thalas and led by the Ranger-General of Silvermoon, leader of the high elves' military forces, and ventured beyond their borders to guard their lands and honor.<ref>[[Feathered Letter]]</ref> During the Third War, this organization was led by [[Sylvanas Windrunner]]. The Elven Ranger Corps met [[Arthas Menethil]] at the borders of Quel'Thalas and fought the traitorous prince every step of the way, through both the Inner and Outer Elfgates, back towards the high elven capital.

Though the Farstriders were a proud group of rangers, many of them were lost with the downfall of their homeland. Their legacy continues to live on through the new generation of rangers trained under the [[Silvermoon Remnant]].<ref>[[Ranger Rubinah Sunsworn#Quotes]]</ref> Under the Remnant, the Farstriders were at first led by [[Damilara Sunsorrow]], though she was replaced as Ranger-General by [[Halduron Brightwing]] following the establishment of the [[Regency Council]].

{{Npcbox | name = Farad Wrightsow | image = Farad Wrightsow.png | level = 25 | faction = Alliance | aggro = {{Aggro|1|-1}}
{{Aggro|-1|-1}} | affiliation = [[Stormwind (faction)|Stormwind]], [[Defias Brotherhood]] | race = Human | creature = Humanoid | gender = Male | location = [[Darkshire]], [[Duskwood]] | status = Killable }} '''Farad Wrightsow''' is a [[human]] found in a shack outside of [[Darkshire]] in [[Duskwood]]. A renowned engineer, along with his friend [[Maltimor Gartside]], the two built the original harvest golems out of their old workshop in [[Moonbrook]] and sold them to the local farmers to help them, as well as to be able to afford to move out of [[Westfall]]. However, due to the farmers' low purchasing power, they sold them as low prices and would lose money on construction. Thus, they designed a killswitch into the golems with enchanted animation runes that when activated would turn the golems into murderous machines, blaming it on the work of a vile warlock and "fixing" the golems for a much higher price. In a fit of greed, Maltimor attempted to kill Farad by activating the golems' killswitch while he was working on them so that he would keep all of the money. Farad survived the attempt on his life, though he was left blinded as a result and was left with a deep hatred for Maltimor. Though Maltimor saw the destruction he caused and sought to reverse it, his spell failed for reasons unknown. Though Maltimor attempted to dissuade him, Farad threw his lot in with the [[Defias Brotherhood]], continuing to produce the animation runes for them with the goblin [[Gazzirik]] as the golems wrecked havoc across the farmlands of [[Westfall]].{{questlong|Alliance|25|The Harvest Golem Mystery (16)|The Harvest Golem Mystery}}{{questlong|Alliance|25|Letter from Maltimor}} ==Quotes== :''Main article: {{questlong|Alliance|25|The Harvest Golem Mystery (16)|The Harvest Golem Mystery}}'' ;Gossip Get out of my shack. ==Drops== * [[Letter from Maltimor (item)]] ==Objective of== * {{questlong|Alliance|25|The Harvest Golem Mystery (16)|The Harvest Golem Mystery}} ==Patch changes== * {{Patch|1.16.1|note=Added.}} ==References== {{reflist}} [[Category:Human characters]] [[Category:Engineers]] [[Category:Duskwood mobs]] [[Category:Defias Brotherhood]]

'''Fel energy''',<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|54|Fel Energy Irregularities III}}</ref> also called '''chaos magic''',<ref>[https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Warcraft_III:_Reign_of_Chaos_Game_Manual#Warlock Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos Game Manual#Warlock]</ref> is demonic [[arcane]] magic.<ref name="Genetic Alteration Anomaly">{{questlong|Alliance|53|Genetic Alteration Anomaly!}}</ref><ref>[[Kil'jaeden and the Shadow Pact]]</ref>

==Characteristics and uses==
[[Blood elves]] are known to use fel magic as an alternative to sate their arcane addiction, although its usage is opposed by the [[high elves]] of the [[Silvermoon Remnant]].<ref>{{questlong|Alliance|9|The Way of Fel}}</ref> The chaotic energies of fel have a corruptive influence on the land, having tainted the regions of [[Felwood]] (which takes its name from the energy that corrupted it)<ref>[[Eridan Bluewind#Quotes]]</ref> and the [[Blasted Lands]]. The magical fluctuations of fel emanating from the [[Dark Portal]] have notably warped the beasts that lurk in the wastes of the Blasted Lands, altering the boars close to the Portal into [[helboar]]s.<ref>[[Engineer Wigglestip#Quotes]]</ref><ref name="Genetic Alteration Anomaly" /><ref>[[Commander Baelos#Quotes]]</ref>

==Warlocks==
Having an innate association with demonology, [[warlock]]s have adopted a connection to the darkest fel energies. Through their understandings of demonology they are able to dominate certain agents of the Burning Legion, such as [[imp]]s, [[voidwalker]]s, [[succubi]], [[felhound]]s, and [[felguard]]s.

He ruled the Wildhammer clan from [[Aerie Peak]] in the [[Hinterlands]] following the departure of [[Kurdran Wildhammer]] and joined his companions [[Rhonin]] and [[Vereesa Windrunner|Vereesa]] in freeing the Dragon Queen [[Alexstrasza]] from [[Grim Batol]]. ==Biography== ===Day of the Dragon=== Falstad Wildhammer was a noble gryphon rider of the [[Wildhammer clan]] of the [[Hinterlands]], commanding a small flight of such riders who patrolled the shores of [[Lordaeron]] for any hostile draconic activity after the [[Second War]]. Falstad and his comrades protected the town of [[Hasic]] from certain doom, and then transported human mage [[Rhonin]] and his companions across the [[Great Sea]] to [[Khaz Modan]]. During the journey, however, the group was ambushed and Falstad's kinsmen were killed. Nevertheless, at the incentive of [[Vereesa Windrunner]], Falstad continued to Khaz Modan. Later, with the help of a clan of hill dwarves, Falstad reached [[Grim Batol]] and fought in the final battle there to free the Red Dragon Queen [[Alexstrasza]]. ===World of Warcraft=== Now High Thane, Falstad appears as a quest giver located at [[Aerie Peak]] in the Hinterlands where he deals with the encroaching forest trolls. ==Quests== * {{questlong|Alliance|43|To The Hinterlands}} {{questfinish}} * {{questlong|Alliance|43|Gryphon Master Talonaxe (quest)|Gryphon Master Talonaxe}} {{queststart}} * {{questlong|Alliance|45|Nat Pagle, Murloc Expert}} {{queststart}} ==Quotes== ;Gossip I am Falstad, Thane of the Wildhammer Clan. [[Image:Falkirs.jpg|thumb|"Harbinger" harboured at Faldir's Cove]]
A small natural harbour on the southern shores of [[Arathi Highlands]], near [[Drowned Reef|The Drowned Reef]].

An expedition of [[Blackwater Raiders]], led by Captain Steelgut, was sent to this land in search of elven treasure. A device made by two gnomish engineers, doctor Draxlegauge and Professor Phizzlethorpe, detected a treasure of elven gems, calcified within the stones of the reef. 

Unfortunately, due to mysterious tide caused by the [[Naga|Nagas]] guarding the sunken ruins, two of the three ships sunk. The third ship, Harbinger, landed safely on the shore, however its crew was trapped in the bay, until some adventurers agreed to fight the Nagas and retrieve the navigation logs off of the sunken ships.

The cove can be reached through a short tunnel south of [[Stromgarde]] walls.

[[image:Faol's Rest.jpg|thumb|Faol's Rest]]
'''Faol's Rest''' is located in eastern [[Tirisfal Glades]], just southwest of the [[Scarlet Monastery]]. It is presumed to be the final resting place of the much revered archbishop [[Alonsus Faol]], who died some time before the coming of the [[Scourge]]. Although the grave was a much visited place by mourners in the time before the [[Plague of Undeath]], it now lies untended and forgotten.

It serves as the [[Graveyard]] for those dying on the Scarlet Monastery [[instance]] or the low-level quests around that place.

[[File:Fargodeep Mine.jpg|thumb|300px|Fargodeep Mine.]]

The '''Fargodeep Mine''' is an abandoned [[gold mine]] located in [[Elwynn Forest]], which has been overrun by a [[Elwynn kobolds|clan of kobolds]].

==Inhabitants==
* {{NPC|Combat|Goldtooth|icon=Kobold}}
* {{NPC|Combat|Narg the Taskmaster|icon=Kobold}} (rare)
* {{NPC|Combat|Kobold Miner|icon=Kobold}}
* {{NPC|Combat|Kobold Tunneler|icon=Kobold}}

==Notes==
* It is a great place to work on professions and collect some much sought after raw materials. Players will probably be around level five or six when first entering the mine, but after completing all the associated quests, they should be around level nine. It usually takes one to one and a half hours to complete all of them. A handy tip is to make certain to carry as many bags as possible because they will fill quickly with loot. Not only will players be tasked with exploring the mine, but they will also gather large candles and gold dust from the kobolds.
* In addition to the mine quests, the [[Stonefield Necklace quest chain|"Lost Necklace"]] quest chain should be worked on at the same time, as it covers the same area. This is begun by talking with [["Auntie" Bernice Stonefield]] located at the [[Stonefield Farm]].The chain will culminate in a fight with [[Goldtooth]], a rather large kobold located deep within the Fargodeep Mine.
* While running through the mine, players should watch for the kobold, [[Narg the Taskmaster]]. He is a level 10 rare mob who may spawn in the back of the mine.

[[Image:Far Watch Post.jpg|thumb|Far Watch Post]]
Far Watch Post is a small outpost of the Horde located just west of the bridge between [[Durotar]] and [[The Barrens]] {{co|62|20|The Barrens}}. It is made up of a watchtower and an orc burrow with its assortment of guards and helpers. A riding wolf pen watched over by a pair of peons is located a bit to the south, but it contains more chickens than wolves. Overall, this is not a very accommodating spot, but necessary for the protection of Durotar from the [[Alliance]] and the [[centaur]] and [[quilboar]] threat of the Barrens.

[[File:Falfarren River.jpg|thumb|Falfarren River]]
The '''Falfarren River''' runs northeast to southwest across [[Ashenvale]], and is considered by many to be the dividing line between the [[night elven]] territory under [[Astranaar]] to the west, and the [[orcish]] territory under [[Splintertree Post]] to the east. The water of the river originates at [[Mount Hyjal]], passes through a series of waterfalls into the lake at [[Xavian]], before it runs between Splintertree and [[Night Run]] southwest. It then runs past the only bridge spanning the Falfarren, continuing between [[Silverwing Outpost]] and the southern [[Moonwell (Ashenvale)|moonwell]] before it slips underground beneath the mountains of the northern [[Barrens]]. Several level 26-27 aggressive [[Bog Beast]] can be found roaming below the surface of the river at sections around [[Felfire Hill]].

I have vision that she lacks...."]] __NOTOC__ '''Fandral Staghelm''' is the current Arch-Druid of the [[Night Elves|Kaldorei]]. Fandral was one of [[Malfurion Stormrage]]'s top lieutenants, and trained many of the newest generation of druids of the wild. His hot temperament has sometimes clashed with the more restrained Malfurion. Fandral believes that the future of the [[Night Elves]] demands more expansionism and military planning. His radical beliefs and aggressive demeanor often lead him to quarrel openly with [[Tyrande]]. With Malfurion missing, Fandral Staghelm - the leader of those who wished to plant the new [[World Tree]] - became the new Arch-Druid. In no time at all, he and his fellow druids had forged ahead and planted the great tree, [[Teldrassil]], off the stormy coasts of northern [[Kalimdor]]. Under their care, the tree sprouted up above the clouds. Among the twilight boughs of the colossal tree, the wondrous city of [[Darnassus]] took root. However, the tree was not consecrated with nature's blessing and soon fell prey to the corruption of the Burning Legion. Now the wildlife, and even the limbs of Teldrassil itself are tainted by a growing darkness. Regardless, to this date Fandral has proven to be an effective replacement for the missing Malfurion in strictly secular and iconic terms- none of Malfurion's confidants are exactly pleased. [[Quintis Jonespyre]], a druid residing in [[Feathermoon Stronghold]] is interested - nay, concerned - with why the Arch Druid in [[Darnassus]] is using the name of the [[Cenarion Circle]], as well as the Circle's resources, to procure vast amounts of [[morrowgrain]]. He is a researcher - curses are his specialty. Quintis has heard that morrowgrain, under the right conditions, exude qualities like other herbs used in primitive curses. ==Lore (History)== The children of [[C'Thun]], the [[Qiraji]], had spent thousands of years building an army capable of exacting revenge upon the whole of [[Kalimdor]] and now the prize was within their grasp. The [[Titan]]s had long since vacated this world. Only the [[night elves]] that once inhabited this area were here to defend. A mighty Qiraji known as [[General Rajaxx]] would command the initial incursion into [[Silithus]]. Only one would stand in his way: The clever night elf [[druid]] known as '''Fandral Staghelm'''. They refer to him as [[Khar'sis]] or 'hand of earth' in the native Qiraji tongue. Staghelm and his armies were clearly overwhelmed as the endless flow of Rajaxx's troops poured into Silithus. It would seem as if Staghelm, however, was more than just a nuisance to the Qiraji. Under Staghelm, the whole of the night elf armies had come together to defend Kalimdor, greatly slowing the Qiraji forces. Unfortunately, the night elven defense was untenable and Rajaxx knew that they could not hold out much longer. Their tenacity, however, was causing great frustration to Rajaxx and causing even more frustration to his kings. [[Vek'nilash]] and [[Vek'lor]], known as the [[Twin Emperors]] of [[Ahn'Qiraj]], watched the war from the sanctuary of their temple. The clever brothers devised a plan to demoralize and divide Staghelm's forces. [[Valstann Staghelm]] served as the right hand of his father Fandral. A proud and noble warrior, his dedication and adoration for his father unyielding... and the Twin Emperors sensed this as weakness. A weakness that could be exploited. The Qiraji forces were commanded to fall back and hide the bulk of their numbers beneath the sands of the desert. A small attack was ordered upon [[Southwind Village]] while the front lines of Staghelm's Army were kept occupied. Valstann, eager to please his father, convinced Fandral to allow him to take a small battalion to the defense of Southwind. Surely with the tide of battle turning their way, no harm could come to his beloved child. The trap was sprung, Valstann was captured by the hiding Qiraji and Southwind Village obliterated. Rajaxx himself would take the captive Valstann to the front lines of the battle where - in front of Staghelm and the night elf forces - he would brutally execute the young night elf. The war continued, but the will of the great leader was sapped. The whole of Silithus was soon engulfed by the Silithid and their Qiraji hosts. Later they were nothing, their defiance defeated. == Quests == Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm starts the following quests: * [[Image:Alliance_15.gif]] [11] [[Quest:Grove of the Ancients|Grove of the Ancients]] * [[Image:Alliance_15.gif]] [50] [[Quest:Un'Goro Soil|Un'Goro Soil]] * [[Image:Alliance_15.gif]] [50] [[Quest:Morrowgrain Research (1)|Morrowgrain Research (1)]] * [[Image:Alliance_15.gif]] [55] [[Quest:The New Frontier (2)|The New Frontier (2)]]

== Objectives ==
Bring 12 Azureshimmer Hippogryph Feathers to Elendon Truebough at Narvalis Point on Moonwhisper Coast. You can find them scattered throughout Moonwhisper Coast.
* [[Azureshimmer Hippogryph Feather]] (12)

== Description ==
Narvalis Point may look quiet, but quiet places still need defenders. Sentinels patrol these woods day and night. Most people see their glaives and forget the other half of their craft.

The bow.

<Elendon lifts a bundle of unfinished arrows from his workbench.>

Good arrows are not simple things. Straight shafts, balanced heads… and proper fletching. Without the right feathers, even the finest arrow will fly crooked. Normally we would import materials from deeper kaldorei lands, but supply lines to this coast are… unreliable.

Fortunately, the forests here offer an alternative. Azureshimmer hippogryphs nest along the cliffs and high branches of the surrounding woods. Their feathers are light, strong, and remarkably stable in flight. Perfect for sentinel arrows.

I only need a handful. Gather twelve of their feathers and bring them to me. Do try not to harm more hippogryphs than necessary. They are proud creatures, and they have lived on this coast far longer than we have.

==Rewards==
* 5100 [[XP]]

== Progress ==
Take care when approaching the hippogryphs. They are not hostile by nature, but they defend their nests fiercely. If one takes flight above you, keep your eyes open. They strike from the air faster than most people expect.

== Completion ==
Ah, excellent feathers.

<Elendon runs one of them between his fingers, testing its strength.>

See the structure along the spine? Flexible, but firm. That is exactly what we need. With these I can finish a proper batch of arrows. The sentinels will appreciate the difference the next time they loose a volley across the treeline.

You have my thanks, <class>.

==Patch changes==

== Objectives ==
Bring 40 Fallen One Heads to Rhys Dawnbreeze in Sunsworn Camp on Moonwhisper Coast.
* [[Fallen One Head]] (40)

== Description ==
The draenei.

Strange beings from a broken world. The same world our traitor prince chose over his own people.

<Rhys spits.>

There is a village to the northeast. They keep to themselves. We traded for their crystals. Curious things. They hum when no wind blows. I do not trust them, but they have not raised steel against us. Not yet.

In the swamps and forests, it is different. Those who call themselves the Fallen Ones stalk the reeds and the tree line. They do not parley. They rush you without warning and strip the flesh from your bones. I have seen what they leave behind.

We cannot build anything here while they breathe. The expedition will never be secure with them prowling our flanks.

Hunt them. Kill them where they hide. Bring me forty of their heads as proof. Yes, forty. Do not question the number. These swamps crawl with them. You will not struggle to find your count.

Thin them out until even the mud runs red.

==Rewards==
* 5800 [[XP]]

== Progress ==
Beware their daggers.

They coat the blades in venom not born of this world. It burns cold in the blood. I have watched strong warriors fall to their knees from a scratch no deeper than a thorn.

Do not trust your armor to save you. Do not trust your healers to mend you in time. Even they struggle against that poison.

== Completion ==
Forty heads.

It brings a measure of peace, seeing them laid out like that. Not enough, but some. We have only carved a dent in their numbers, nothing more.

Still, it should give them pause. Fear lingers longer than pain, and they are not brave creatures when faced with open slaughter.

With luck, it will be enough to keep them from testing our encampment while we are still here.

== Objectives ==
Report to Cairne Bloodhoof in Elders’ Rise, Thunder Bluff, Mulgore.

== Description ==
My father was skeptical enough when we received news of an agreement between the Bloodhoof and the Moonhoof, truth be told. The Moonhoof have always favored their independence and, above all, their relationship with the night elves. The Moonhoof were under the umbrella of the Cenarion Circle.

Both the Grove of the Moon and the Grove of the Sun were there to prove that. To hear that the Grove of the Moon has gone astray is most curious. From what you are telling me, they have abandoned their worship of Mu’sha and traded it for the worship of Lo’sho, which the Elder Moonhoof believes to be a corruption.

I must mull over these things. You will find my father in Elders’ Rise in Thunderbluff. I doubt he will turn you away; he does want the Moonhoof to officially become part of the Horde, especially now that they have estranged themselves from the night elves. I believe this will lead to forced isolation, and the Elder is simply using the Horde to obtain what he needs for it to be so.
